provider: ghproxy mirrors (ghproxy.net, ghfast.top) — free anonymous GitHub raw/release proxy

free_tier.stated: No quota; it proxies raw.githubusercontent.com and release assets, so the ceiling is GitHub's own (100 MiB/repo file, ~1.95 TiB/release). Probed a 50,901,339-byte GitHub file through ghproxy.net: HTTP 200, correct Content-Length.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that no cap exists
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: no retention statement was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that retention is unlimited
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Free, anonymous, no key. These are community-run mirrors of the GitHub CDN, funded by volunteers — hence the polyculture of hostnames (gh-proxy.com, ghproxy.net, ghfast.top, gh.api.99988866.xyz) and the constant churn.

tooling: Prefix form: https://ghproxy.net/https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<ref>/<path> and .../https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/<tag>/<asset>. Nothing else to install.
chaining: A fourth free mirror for the same GitHub origin, and the only one that also carries *release assets* (which jsDelivr cannot see and raw.githack cannot serve). For a 20 TiB archive of 2 GiB release assets, rotating across ghproxy.net / ghfast.top / raw.githack / jsDelivr / Fastly's release-asset CDN gives five independent read paths over one storage bill.
limits_note: per-ip-shaping is the real constraint — measured ~128 KB/s (7.1 MB in 55 s) on a 50 MB fetch, versus 11.3 MB/s from hop.js and 6.4 MB/s from jsDelivr. Rule 6 applies: measure a baseline before blaming the origin.
reliability_note: Volunteer infrastructure, high churn — of four mirrors tested this session, gh-proxy.com and cdn.gitmirror.com failed to resolve/connect while ghproxy.net and ghfast.top both returned the full file. Treat as a bandwidth multiplier for large files, never as an availability guarantee. Their own issue trackers document the churn (hunshcn/gh-proxy#116 mirror list, 'ghproxy.com 打不开了').
